== Course of events ==

The Mouse, having spent considerable effort in an attempt to bore the assembled company dry with a recitation of William the Conqueror's history, abandons that tedious enterprise and offers instead to share something of its own. It promises to tell its sad history—a tale touching upon the Mouse's own sorrows rather than the dreary chronicles of ancient kings. Yet when Alice, in her curious and sometimes wayward fashion, misunderstands what the Mouse intends to convey, the creature's disposition transforms entirely. The Mouse grows angry, its willingness to confide undone by Alice's misapprehension. What began as a moment of promised intimacy becomes instead one of wounded indignation.
